summary: This version of the coffee program checks its arguments before doing any work: if the coffee type is missing or the shot count is less than one, it throws an IllegalArgumentException and stops. The first call brews normally, and the second call deliberately passes 0 shots so you can see the error halt the program.

lines.code: // This call will throw the particular error
lines.text: The second call is here on purpose. It shows what happens when a bad value arrives from another system, such as an inventory check that reports zero shots available.

lines.code: throw new IllegalArgumentException("Coffee type must not be null or blank.");
lines.text: Throwing is the opposite of catching: instead of recovering, the method refuses to continue and hands the problem back to its caller. IllegalArgumentException is Java's standard way to say a value passed in was not acceptable.
Guard checks like this sit at the very top of the method, before any brewing happens, so the method never does half the work with data it cannot use.

lines.code: System.out.println("🔮 Brewing " + type + " with " + shots + " shot(s)...");
lines.text: Nothing below the guards runs unless both checks pass, which is why the output shows the Espresso brewing in full and then stops abruptly on the Latte.
With two shots the magic power is 84, so the boost message appears; a single shot would fall below the threshold of 50 and skip it.
